source.title: Champions League Performance Insight: Arsenal's right-sided overload — clip 1

situation.outcome: Rice draws out a defender, Saka runs into the opened space and crosses for Havertz to score
situation.human_observation: Per UEFA's technical analysis unit, Arsenal's game plan against Sporting CP was to force Sporting into a flat back five and exploit the space either side of Sporting's midfield two (Morita and Hjulmand) within their 5-2-3 defensive shape, with the right flank in particular targeted for overloads and combinations — the source of Arsenal's two early goals. In this specific clip, Arsenal's attack builds down the right with a structured push toward the defensive line involving five players. Declan Rice moves into the right channel, drawing out Sporting's left-sided centre-back, Gonçalo Inácio. Rice's movement opens space for Saka, who capitalises with a well-timed run and delivers a cross that Kai Havertz converts.
situation.priority_problem: How to use a central midfielder's (Rice's) deliberate movement into a wide channel to drag a covering centre-back out of position, creating the space for a winger (Saka) to attack and deliver a cross for a converted chance.
visible_evidence: Arsenal commit five players in a structured push toward Sporting's defensive line down the right side.
Declan Rice moves from central midfield into the right channel.
This movement draws Sporting's left-sided centre-back, Gonçalo Inácio, out of his defensive line to follow/engage Rice.
The space vacated by Inácio's movement is exploited by Saka.
Saka makes a well-timed run into that space.
Saka delivers a cross from the resulting position.
Kai Havertz converts the cross to score.

coaching.objective: Use a central midfielder's movement into a wide channel to deliberately draw a covering centre-back out of the defensive line, creating space for a winger to attack in behind and deliver a cross for a teammate to finish.
coaching.practice_design: Positional/rondo-to-goal practice against a back-five or back-four shape: attacking side commits players (structured five-player push, as in this clip) toward one side of the pitch. A central midfielder is coached to time a run into the wide channel specifically to occupy/drag a covering centre-back, rather than to receive the ball directly. As the centre-back engages, the wide attacker (winger) times a run into the space just vacated, receives, and delivers a cross for an onrushing striker to finish. Progress from unopposed shape work to opposed practice with a defined defensive block (e.g. 5-2-3) to replicate the real spacing being exploited.
success_cues: Central midfielder's run into the channel is deliberate and draws the covering centre-back out of position, rather than being incidental.
The vacated space is recognised and attacked promptly by the winger.
Winger's run is well-timed to arrive in space rather than into a marked position.
Cross is delivered with enough quality for the target striker to convert.
The wider structural push (numbers committed to that side) is maintained throughout the sequence, not abandoned once the ball starts moving.
